seoDescription: Learn how to create an adorable jellyfish charm using a Rainbow Loom in this easy-to-follow tutorial. This DIY guide walks you through the entire process, from setting up your loom and placing the bands to form the body, to creating the long, flowing tentacles. You'll master the hooking process, learn how to add cute black bands for eyes, and finish with a secure slip knot. Perfect for beginners and experienced loomers alike, this project results in a super cute Rainbow Loom jellyfish charm you can use as a keychain or accessory.

chapters.description: The creator introduces the jellyfish charm and lists all the necessary materials for the project.

chapters.title: Placing the Body Bands
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to start placing double bands on the loom to form the top part of the jellyfish body.

chapters.title: Creating and Attaching Side Tentacles
chapters.description: Learn how to wrap a single band to create a small side tentacle and then attach it to the side of the loom.

chapters.title: Placing the Main Tentacles & Cap Bands
chapters.description: This section covers laying out the long single-band chains for the main tentacles and securing them with cap bands.

chapters.title: Adding Eyes and Horizontal Bands
chapters.description: Learn how to wrap black bands to create the eyes and add the single horizontal bands to hold the body together.

chapters.title: Hooking the Tentacles
chapters.description: The hooking process begins by pulling the eye loops over and then hooking the long, single-chain tentacles from the bottom up.

chapters.title: Hooking the Body & Tying the Slip Knot
chapters.description: This chapter covers how to hook the main body of the jellyfish, close off the design, and secure everything with a slip knot.

chapters.title: Finishing and Shaping the Jellyfish
chapters.description: After removing the charm from the loom, learn how to adjust the tentacles, shape the body, and hide the slip knot's loose end.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.description: The creator shows off the final jellyfish charm and provides a closing message with calls to action.

summary:
## Key Concepts: Rainbow Loom Jellyfish Charm

This document outlines the key steps to create a jellyfish charm using a Rainbow Loom.

### Materials Needed

*   **Loom**: Any type of Rainbow Loom.
*   **Hook**: A Rainbow Loom hook (metal tip is recommended).
*   **Bands**:
    *   55 bands for the jellyfish body (e.g., dual-layer Sweets collection).
    *   2 black bands for the eyes.

### Loom Setup (Arrows Pointing Down)

1.  **Body Top (Double Bands)**: 
    *   Start at the top center pin, placing two bands vertically down.
    *   From the second pin, place two bands diagonally to the left and two to the right, creating a pinwheel shape.
    *   Place three sets of vertical double bands down the center column.
    *   Lay two more rows of vertical double bands across all three columns.

2.  **Side Tentacles**: 
    *   Wrap one **single band** around your hook 3 times to create a cap band.
    *   Pull this cap band onto two bands.
    *   Place this piece vertically on the outer left pins, next to the body.
    *   Repeat for the right side.

3.  **Main Tentacles (Single Bands)**:
    *   Take one **single band** at a time and place vertical bands down each of the three columns.
    *   Stop before the very last row of pins; leave it empty.

4.  **Cap Bands**: 
    *   On the last pin of each tentacle chain, wrap one **single band** around the pin 3 times. Do this for all three columns.

5.  **Eyes**: 
    *   On the pins directly above where the side tentacles are attached, wrap one **black band** around each pin 4 times.

6.  **Horizontal Bands**:
    *   Place one **single band** across the top three pins of the body.
    *   Place another single band across the next set of three pins.
    > [!IMPORTANT]
    > For the last horizontal band, place it on the left pin, wrap it *around* the center pin, and then stretch it to the right pin.

### Hooking Process

1.  **Secure the Eyes**: Using your hook, pull the four black loops of each eye over the top of the pin to cinch them onto the band below.

2.  **Hook the Tentacles**: 
    *   Go inside the cap band on each of the three bottom pins.
    *   Grab the bottom single band and hook it forward.
    *   Continue this single-chain hooking process all the way up for all three tentacles.

3.  **Hook the Body**:
    *   Go inside the side-tentacle loops and the horizontal band, grab only the bottom two body bands, and hook them forward. The side tentacle loops themselves remain unhooked.
    *   Continue hooking the vertical double bands up towards the center.

4.  **Close the Body**: 
    *   Hook the top-left and top-right bands inward to the center pin.
    *   Hook the final set of two bands from the center pin forward.

5.  **Tie a Slip Knot**: 
    *   Stay on the outside of the final pin and grab the bottom two bands.
    *   Pull them over the top two bands and off the pin.
    *   Gently tug the remaining loop to tighten it.

### Finishing Touches

1.  **Remove from Loom**: Carefully pull the entire creation off the loom.
2.  **Adjust**: 
    *   Straighten the tentacle bands if they are twisted.
    *   Gently pull on the small side tentacles to make them more prominent.
    *   Stretch and shape the top part of the jellyfish body.
3.  **Hide the Tail**: Use your hook to tuck the loose end of the slip knot into the body of the jellyfish.

## Introduction & Materials

Hi everyone, it's Tutorials by A here and today I'll be showing you how to create these super cute little jellyfish. And basically this is a quite easy design, I don't think it's super duper difficult, so hopefully a lot of you guys will be able to make it. Don't forget to give this video a big thumbs up before we get started. And now without further ado, let's move on to the materials needed. 

So today you will need any type of loom and you will also need a hook. I'll be using a Rainbow Loom metal tip hook today. You will need two bands of black for the eyes, as well as 55 bands of your choice of color for the body. Today I'll be using the rainbowloom.com online exclusive Sweets collection bands and they basically are dual layers, so they've got two rings of color on the band, and I just think they look super cool and I think they'll look great with the jellyfish. 

And my loom today has two red arrows because I took apart my looms and put all the pin bars in different looms and stuff like that. So that's why I just happened to accidentally put one of my red arrow pin bars right here. So your loom will have no red arrow like that if you plan on buying one or anything like that. So anyways all my supplies today are from rainbowloom.com and now without further ado let's get started.

## Placing the Body Bands

So I'm just going to start with my loom's arrows pointing down and we're going to start at the top of our loom by placing two bands. And you're going to place those vertically. For the first part of this project, we're always going to be using two bands at a time. I'll let you guys know when we are going to switch over to just using one band at a time. Now I'm taking two bands here and I'm going to put these here on the left. And we're going to use two again for the right, so that way we've kind of got this pinwheel kind of shape here.

Then we're going to use double bands still and go vertically three times here. So here is the first one. Oh goodness, I let go of those ones. Let's see, try this again. Here are the second set, and then my third set are right here. So you should have something like this.

Now we're going to do two more rows of vertical bands using two bands at a time. So do that two more times. So just going across using two bands at a time. So I've got one row here, we're going to do that one more time.

## Creating and Attaching Side Tentacles

Just like that. So now when you're finished, we are now going to add on the little parts here that stick out on the side of the jellyfish. So you're going to take one single orange band, or whatever color you happen to be using, and you're going to wrap that around your hook three times. So that way you get something like this. And it does not matter the direction in which you twist the band, I just twisted it like this. Then you're going to take double bands, slide those onto your hook. Let me get that out of the frame since the camera keeps focusing on that. And then you're going to grab these three rings here and pull through, so that way you've got this here. Then we're going to go back to our loom and place these over here across these two pins here. So the bottom end goes here, the other end is going to go here. And it doesn't really matter which end goes where as long as it's vertically right between those two pins.

Okay, so now we're going to do the same exact thing for the right side. So I'm going to take a single band and wrap this around my hook three times again. And I feel like my lighting on my camera changed for some reason, but here's that. Then I'm going to take double bands, two bands at a time, put those on my hook so I can slide these three rings up and onto those double bands there, so that way you get something like this. Then we're going to put these across the two right pins here, just like that. So now you should have something like this.

## Placing the Main Tentacles & Cap Bands

Now we're going to add the single chains that make the tentacles, and we're going to have three. You can also layer them on top to make more tentacles, but we're just going to stick with three today. So for this, we are now going to use one band at a time and we're going to go vertically on each pin bar all the way down to the end of our loom except when it comes to the last set of pins you're going to put no bands on. So you're going to put them all the way down your loom except for the very last band. So you're going to skip the very last band. So not going to go super slow for this part just because it's pretty easy. You're just going to go vertically all the way down and then when I get to the bottom you'll see what I mean by not putting on bands for the last set of pins because that might be a little bit confusing to explain. So just keep going all the way down your loom.

So I'm here at the last set of pins that I'm going to be putting bands on. Okay, so as you can see here, this is what I meant by not putting on any more bands at the end. We are not going to put any bands on these three pins or sets here. So you're almost all the way down to the bottom but you've just skipped one row. So let's add the cap bands onto these very bottom pins here. So you're going to need three bands for this. You're going to take one single band, wrap it around each of these three pins three times. So here I go one, two, and three. Just like that. Same thing for the next two. One, two, and three. And it doesn't matter what directions you twist these in. Two and three. So when you're finished, your loom should look like this on the bottom. We've got cap bands on each of these.

## Adding Eyes and Horizontal Bands

And now we're going to go up to the very top of our loom and we're going to add on the eyes. So for this you're going to need your two black bands. We're going to go to these two pins right here, as you can see, it's the pin that's above here where these little rings are that we put on earlier right here. So right here, I'm going to wrap this around four times. So, one, two, three, and four. So I've got one eye on. You're going to take your remaining black band and wrap that four times around on the opposite side. So one, two, three and four. So now I have something like this on my loom. So just check and make sure that that's what you've got while I get some more bands out.

And now we are going to do the last step, which is adding our horizontal bands. So you're going to take one single band of whatever color you are using for your body here and you're going to just put that across these three pins just like that. And then do the same thing for the next three. And for this last set of three pins that we're going to add this on, you're going to put it on the very left one. However, for the next pin, you're going to go around it like that and then place the other end right here on the right, so that way you get something like this. So one more check over before we go ahead and start the hooking process.

## Hooking the Tentacles

So just make sure that your loom looks something like this, and if so, we can now start the hooking process. So we're going to start with the eyes real quick and what we're going to do is we're going to grab these black loops right here, pull them over the pin so that way it cinches this band here. So it doesn't matter how many you grab at once. Definitely if you have a plastic hook, grab one or two first. So you can grab this one, pull that over the pin and release. Make sure you're not going inside of any bands, you're staying on the outside, grabbing those and pulling those over just like that. So that way it cinches right here in the middle. Then we're going to do the same thing for the other side. Doesn't matter again how many you pull over at once, I just happen to grab all of them on that one. So as you can see, I've pulled my eyes over here so they're cinched there.

And now we can start the hooking process for the entire jellyfish. So it doesn't matter what order you hook these in. You can hook one all the way up and then do the rest or you can just go one by one here. I'm just going to go and do one on each. So you're going to continue this process of hooking these single chains all the way up. And again, I'm not going to go too slow for this part just because it's not super difficult to do this, because it's just single chains, the most basic bracelet for Rainbow Loom. But just make sure that you're going inside the pin and grabbing that very bottom band only.

## Hooking the Body & Tying the Slip Knot

Okay, so I have now finished hooking all of the single chains that run up and down my loom for the most part of my loom. If you're not to this point yet, then please feel free to pause the video until you're caught up to this point. And if you're here, then let's go ahead and work on the body. 

So as for these bands here that have the loops around them, we are not going to be hooking these; they're going to be left unhooked. So what you want to do is go inside the top three layers of bands, so you're going inside these bands with the loops here too, and then you're only going to grab the bottom two bands here and hook those forward just like that. As for the center, it's just kind of more normal. You're just hooking the bottom two here over. And for this side, it's exactly the same as this side. Go inside the top three layers and grab only the bottom two layers just like that. So these bands that are here stuck out on the sides are not hooked. 

Now we are going to go ahead and hook up. So just make sure you're going inside of all the bands except for the bottom two and then you're grabbing the bottom two and hooking those forward like this. And then we're going to do the same thing for the next row grabbing the bottom two and hooking forward just like that.

So when you're to this point here, it's now time to close this off. So we're going to go on the left side, hook this side inwards here. And then we're going to go on the right side and hook that inwards as well, so that way all our bands are now on this middle pin. Lastly, we are just going to go inside all the bands except for the bottom two, then we're grabbing the bottom two and hooking those forward just like that.

So now all of our bands are attached with this here. We're now going to tie a slip knot. You can also add a C-clip on it here but I just want to tie it off with just my bands. So you're going to go in and grab the bottom two here. Make sure you're not going inside the band, you're staying on the outside and grabbing these bottom two, pull that over the pin and release. Then you're going to grab the bands that are still on the pin and give those a little tug to tighten. And then we've now completed that slip knot. So before you remove everything from your loom, just go ahead and make sure that your loom looks something like this. And if so, we are now going to remove everything off of our loom.

## Finishing and Shaping the Jellyfish

So hot off my loom, this is what the jellyfish looks like. A little bit crazy right now, but that's okay. So if you have any bands that are twisted that were part of the single chain, go ahead and fix those so that way your tentacles aren't super duper curly. If you want them to be curly, then you can go ahead and leave them like that, but I personally want them to be straighter and more even.

Okay, so as you can see we've got these two ends right here that stick off on the sides, but I'm going to go ahead and pull those out because they're not too prominent. So you want to find where those loops are on the sides and just pull those outwards so that way you can make them stick out a little bit more. And then you can go ahead and stretch out the top part to make it shaped as how you'd like. Then I'm going to just take my hook, and I'm going to tuck in these ends right here. So I'm just going to go in through the top layer of single chain bands and kind of put my hook inside so that way I can reach up for those bands right here and then pull this through my project so that way these bands are hidden. And give that a little bit of a tug so that way it's not all scrunched up there.

## Conclusion

And after that, after you've fixed everything that is here on your project we are now finished with this really cool jellyfish charm. So anyways, that is how you create this super cute little jellyfish charm.
